sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Ansar Allah Health Ministry via Reuters, Nov 8 03:13+03:00] Airstrikes on homes in al-Shariya village, Bani Hushaysh district, ~15km northeast of Sanaa, on Saturday killed at least 33 people and wounded 39, most of them women and children -- up from 27 killed / 36 wounded recorded at totw-20261107-2200-01. Toll progression in ~12 hours: 22 (AP, Saturday afternoon) -> 25 (Al-Masirah, evening) -> 27 (Reuters/AP, late evening) -> 33 (Reuters, Nov 8 early hours). Hospital director Abdul-Aziz al-Dailami: many victims remained trapped under rubble, including first responders; follow-up strikes targeted paramedics (recorded 1900-03). [ATTRIBUTION UNVERIFIED] The Ansar Allah-run Saba news agency blames Saudi airstrikes; Reuters could not independently verify; Saudi Arabia's Center for International Communication said it was investigating. [FIGURE DISCREPANCY -- UNRESOLVED] Al Jazeera's Nov 8 liveblog recap says 32 killed; Roya News English's graphic says 31 killed; Reuters' 33 is the latest wire figure and is used, with the 31/32 variants noted. [CONTEXT] One of the deadliest reported attacks since fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Ansar Allah resumed in July; the 2022 UN-brokered truce is shattered; UN: >1,600 killed and 300,000+ displaced since fighting resumed. Ansar Allah retaliation (six claimed missile/drone operations incl. Riyadh airport and Aramco sites) recorded at totw-20261107-2100-01.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct publisher families for the event and toll trajectory (Reuters T1 + AP T1); the 33 figure itself is Reuters-only.
sections.what_disputed: Saudi Arabia has not confirmed carrying out the strikes; Saudi Center for International Communication says it is investigating (Reuters). The Friday Taiz market strike (30 killed) is still mutually blamed -- Ansar Allah blame Saudi airstrikes, Yemen's government forces blame a Ansar Allah ballistic missile -- showing attribution in this war is routinely contested. Toll figures disagree across outlets (Reuters 33, AJ recap 32, Roya 31).
sections.why_matters: 33 dead near Sanaa -- the toll climbed 22 to 33 in twelve hours while Riyadh stays silent.
